name: Lokalise - Auto-tag to_review on New Key or EN Source Edit
description: Webhook-driven: on a new Lokalise key or an EN source-language edit in any project, adds the to_review tag to that key (merge_tags, skipped if already tagged) and flags its existing target translations as unverified.

parameters.content:
## Setup - register the webhook per project

Easiest way: run the companion workflow **Lokalise - Register to_review Webhook in All Projects**. It does every project at once and is safe to re-run.

Manual way, per project: More > Settings > Webhooks > Add webhook

URL: https://efuturemedia.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/lokalise-to-review

Events to tick (only these two exist as subscriptions):
- New key added (project.key.added)
- Translation updated (project.translation.updated)

Lokalise sends the bulk variants (project.keys.added, project.translations.updated) under those same two subscriptions, and this workflow handles all four payload shapes.

The project ID is read out of each payload, so one URL serves every project.

## What counts as needs review

1. Any newly added key.
2. Any translation update where the language ISO starts with en and the value actually changed (the EN source edit).

Target-language edits are ignored, so the unverified writes this workflow makes cannot re-trigger it.

To change the tag name or the source-language prefix, edit TAG / SOURCE_PREFIX at the top of Normalize Lokalise Events and Decide Tag Actions.

## Writes back to Lokalise

- to_review is added with merge_tags: true, so existing tags survive.
- Keys that already carry to_review are filtered out, so nothing is re-tagged.
- Every non-source translation that has content and is not already unverified gets the Unverified flag, which is what puts it back in the linguists' review queue.

If you ever want tag-only behaviour, disconnect List Target Translations.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ keys: [ Object.assign({ key_id: Number($('Merge Key Ids').item.json.keyId), tags: [ $('Merge Key Ids').item.json.screenTag, 'has_screenshot' ], merge_tags: true }, $('Merge Key Ids').item.json.writeDescription ? { description: $('Merge Key Ids').item.json.description } : {}) ] }) }}

parameters.content:
## Screenshot + screen tag + description

Runs for every key the webhook reports, in any project, right after the to_review decision.

**How the screen is chosen (no Figma access needed):**
1. `Find Sibling Screens` pulls the project's keys that already carry `has_screenshot` (one request, limit 500).
2. `Pick Best Screen` scores each candidate screenshot by how many leading `::` segments its keys share with the new key (squared, so a 3-segment match beats three 1-segment matches). Highest score wins, vote count breaks ties.
3. Keys that already have a screenshot, or whose namespace has no screenshotted sibling, are left untouched.

**Writes:** `key_ids` on the screenshot are MERGED, never replaced. Tags are added with `merge_tags`. The description is only written when the key has none, so hand-written context is never overwritten.

**No Figma links in the description** - freelancers have no Figma access, so the description names the screen and points at the attached screenshot instead: `Seen on: About us (desktop). See the attached screenshot.`

Coverage depends on a Figma backfill having run for that product first - see claude/chatai-figma-screenshots-backfill-2026-08-21.md and claude/figma-file-map.md.

activeVersion.name: Find siblings via screenshots, not our own tag
activeVersion.description: has_screenshot gets stripped by the repo import (keys came back tagged develop/z_human with to_review and has_screenshot removed), so filtering keys by that tag returned nothing and no new key got a screenshot. Sibling lookup now reads the project's screenshots endpoint for the authoritative key_ids, then fetches just those keys by id. Independent of any tag we write.
